title: `sober status`, `sober logs` and the run panel say which host and model ran the node
name: `sober status`, `sober logs` and the run
description:
With three hosts on one board, a run that says only `running` is unreadable. The run record already carries `host` (packages/schema/src/run.ts) and after `resolve-host` it is the resolved one; this node puts it on every surface that shows a run:
- `sober status` and `sober status <node>`: the tier and the host beside a running or finished node (packages/core/src/status.ts, packages/cli/src).
- `sober logs <node>`: a header line before the tail — tier, host, model, started at.
- the dashboard run panel and logs view (apps/dashboard/src/logs, apps/dashboard/src/panel): the same line at the top.

What can be shown as a separate model name depends on the `tier-host-shape` decision: a command line is shown whole; a pair is shown as two words. If the `unnamed-tier` decision is the fallback, the line says `(default host)` so a typo in a tier key is visible.

Tests with the code: one status test, one logs test, one dashboard data test.

brief.approach:
Most of this already exists. The run record carries `host` (the resolved command line, so the model travels inside it, per ADR 0058/0061), plus `tier` and `fallback`. `sober logs <node>` already prints `ran <host> (<tier text>)` (`packages/cli/src/work.ts` `logs()`, ~line 448), and the dashboard logs screen shows the same through `LogWindow.ran` + `ranWith` (`apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts`). The gaps: `sober status` never says what ran a node, and the tier wording is copied by hand in two places.

1. One wording. Add `ranLabel({ tier, fallback }): string` to `packages/schema` in a new small module (e.g. `packages/schema/src/ran.ts`, exported from `index.ts`). It returns exactly today's strings:
   - `unscored`
   - `no model covers this score, fallback to dispatch.host`
   - `<tier> named no host, fallback to dispatch.host`
   - `<tier>`
   schema is the package both the CLI and the browser may import (ADR 0008). Use it in `work.ts` `logs()` and in `ranWith` in `apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts`, deleting both inline copies. Add a test beside it covering the four cases.
2. `sober status`. In `packages/cli/src/status.ts`, where `waiting()` falls back to `run <id>` for a live run (~line 111), print `run <id> · <host> (<ranLabel>)`, using `lastRun(board, id)`, which is already imported. For a node whose last run finished and which is `in-review`, show the same `<host> (<ranLabel>)` in dim text so a reviewer sees what produced the work. `sober status <node>` gets the line from the same helper. Keep the existing `columns()` layout. If the line is too wide, put it on its own indented second line rather than adding a column.
3. The node panel (`apps/dashboard/src/panel/`) is out of scope unless the board payload it already receives carries the last run's host. Check `panel/data.ts`. If it does not, leave the panel alone: the logs screen already shows the line and session-shell adds the model badge. Do not add a wire field for this.
4. No `model` field and no schema change to `run.ts` / `wire.ts`. session-shell derives the model and provider from the host command line (`--model X` / `-m X` / `provider/model`).

acceptance.proves: ranLabel returns the four existing wordings

acceptance.run: ! grep -n 'named no host, fallback' packages/cli/src/work.ts apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts
acceptance.proves: the wording lives in one place, not copied into the CLI and the dashboard
sober status now says what ran a node

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run apps/dashboard/src/logs packages/cli && pnpm --filter @besober/cli typecheck && pnpm --filter @besober/dashboard typecheck
acceptance.proves: existing logs and CLI tests still pass and both packages type-check

acceptance.run: npx biome check packages/schema/src packages/cli/src apps/dashboard/src/logs
